w:r.w:t: Task Work Surface, Proof Submission, Completion/Failure/Blocker Feedback, Validation, and Next-Task Continuation

This document defines the Task Execution and Feedback screens for Torgima Phase 1. These screens are where the user performs the current order, submits proof, reports completion, records failure or blockers, and returns execution reality into the system loop.

The task screen must make execution clear and feedback honest. It must not allow fake completion, missing proof, duplicate submissions, or stale order updates. It must support completed, partially completed, failed, blocked, and skipped states according to backend rules.
Rule: A task does not become real execution until the feedback flow submits valid feedback through the Feedback Processing Engine.
The task screen turns instruction into action; the feedback screen turns action into system truth.
The UI should make the next step obvious, the proof requirement clear, and the feedback path honest enough for Torgima to adapt.

5. What These Screens Do Not Own
They do not mark orders complete locally.
They do not validate proof truth beyond client-side format checks.
They do not calculate signal, condition, rewards, identity, or next task.
They do not allow submission for stale or superseded orders.
They do not call internal feedback or engine routes.
They do not hide rejected proof or validation errors.

The Task Execution and Feedback screens are where Torgima's loop becomes real. The user sees the work, does the work, tells the truth about what happened, and the system responds. The screen must make honest execution easier than fake completion.
